evidence: Heard, alongside Marshall Jefferson, Adonis, and Phuture's DJ Pierre, is documented as one of the Chicago producers who brought Hardy acetates and reel-to-reel dubs of new tracks to debut at the Music Box in the mid-1980s.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Heard's record is slower and softer than most of what Hardy played, which is itself part of the story: the Music Box could break a record that didn't sound like everything else in the room.

explanation.age7: Larry Heard brought his new songs to Ron Hardy, who played them for the crowd at the Music Box before they were even officially released.
explanation.age13: Heard was one of several Chicago producers who gave Hardy early copies of tracks on tape or acetate to test out on the Music Box dancefloor before pressing them.
explanation.adult: This test-the-record-at-the-club-first pipeline is one of the clearest structural facts about how Chicago house records got made: the DJ, not a label, was the first filter.
